newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Zurich group has agreed to acquire Scudder, Stevens & Clark to create a global investment firm in a deal valued at more than $2 billion.
* NationsBank is in talks to acquire investment bank Montgomery Securities Inc for about $1 billion.
* Intel and Digital Equipment Corp are in talks aimed at settling Digital's patent-infringement lawsuit against Intel, sources said.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission is looking at the practice of "pay-to-play" in the public-retirement business.
* Mutual funds continue to be popular spots for investors money.
* Rhone-Poulenc is planning to launch a $4.3 billion bid for full control of its U.S. drug unit, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
* Negotiators involved the tobacco settlement talks faced criticism and questioning from members of the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee.
* In an effort to woo advertisers to the Internet, Web sites are offering free ad space unless it produces a sale.
* OPEC ministers ended talks with a new freeze on its production limits.
* A unit of General Re Corp was ordered to pay a criminal fine of $20.5 million and its former chief executive was sentenced to nearly five years in prison as part of a fraud case.
* The Dow Jones Industrials dropped 35.73 points, closing at 7654.25.
* Heard on the Street: James Gipson, a money manager, is showing grit by holding a hoard of cash s he searches for valued stocks.
* Credit Markets: Treasury bond prices slipped Thursday as a flurry of corporate-debt issues diverted investors' attention from government paper.
